5 commits). This branch fixes two production incidents in a workstation "banc d'essai" (skill-improvement
rail): (1) an import marker that permanently sealed a recoverable failure (server/cli/evalsReconciler.ts,
RETRYABLE_ON_FAILURE_KINDS), (2) a provenance-check false positive in a local LLM judge that rejected honest
citations due to JSON escaping + typographic punctuation (server/services/reviews/localJudge.ts,
normalizeForProvenance / decodeJsonlStringValues), plus two follow-up chip fixes: (3) a git-merge
"unrelated histories" failure when applying skill-improvement branches, fixed by a hand-built two-parent
merge commit that mechanically confines its tree diff to <skill>/ (server/services/reviews/apply.ts,
graftSkillContent — uses raw git plumbing: rm -r, checkout, write-tree, commit-tree), and (4) two race
conditions in a CLI "wait for a hub conversation to be answered" command (server/cli/convo.ts, wakeReason —
removed a stale baseline-comparison mechanism in favor of a pure function of the current snapshot). Docs
were updated in docs/evals/*.md and docs/decision-hub.md to match.
Read the full changed files + their callers/siblings, AND read the MOST-BOUNDED/safest sibling of any
git-plumbing call, marker/lock pattern, or CLI exit-code contract you touch, so you know THIS repo's idiom.
For any file/function that is WHOLLY NEW in this diff (e.g. graftSkillContent, decodeJsonlStringValues,
RETRYABLE_ON_FAILURE_KINDS), audit it standalone — there is no old behavior to diff against. For a
pre-existing function changed by this diff (wakeReason, normalizeForProvenance, mergeApprovedBranchIntoMain,
cmdImport's catch block), scope to what the diff changed vs main, but verify the new behavior against EVERY
call site and EVERY code path (success AND failure) of that function, not just the one path the commit
message describes.
A finding is reportable if it fails ANY gate:
  • CORRECTNESS: some input makes it wrong / crash / lose data (triggerable), OR
  • CONVENTION/SCALABILITY/PLATFORM-LIMIT: it deviates from an idiom that ALREADY exists in this repo
    (cite the sibling file:line that does it right), violates an external hard limit, or is an unbounded
    read / full-table scan / N+1 / over-fetch — EVEN IF today's data makes it work.
  • WIRING: new/changed enforcement/tooling code (marker files that gate at-most-once application, a
    provenance security check, a git-merge safety boundary, a CLI exit-code contract) that does not
    actually fire against this repo's real data shapes/paths, or is not wired into every place the same
    invariant should hold (e.g. is the graft's path-safety guard checked BEFORE every destructive git
    call, not just the first one? does the marker-retry logic apply to every code path that can throw?).
  • STATE-SAFETY: a gate/marker/lock that can be satisfied without the protected work happening, that can
    be bypassed by a crafted input (e.g. a skill name, a candidate id), that leaves the repo/data in a
    half-mutated state on a mid-operation crash, or that can block forever (no escape hatch / re-entrancy
    guard). This is CENTRAL to this diff: it is exactly the class of bug (a marker/gate posed before a
    side-effect, never retired on failure) that motivated the whole chantier — verify the NEW code doesn't
    reintroduce a narrower version of the SAME defect it fixes (e.g. does graftSkillContent's git plumbing
    leave the integration clone in a half-reset state on a partial failure? does the new judge-local-adjacent
    change interact badly with the STILL-UNFIXED judge-local-markers "judging" stuck-state defect, already
    flagged as a separate known chip?).
"Returns correct output today / not triggerable" is NOT grounds to drop a convention/scalability/
platform-limit/wiring/state-safety finding — those are precisely what a review bot flags. Refute
ONLY pure style (naming/formatting/taste/restated guards).

DIMENSION: Is every changed function's new behavior wired into EVERY call site (not just the one the commit message describes)? Does any doc (docs/evals/*.md, docs/decision-hub.md) now assert something the code does not actually do (stale/aspirational documentation)? Does convo.ts's wakeReason removal of baselineFollowup leave any dead reference/import? Any orphan reference to a removed concept (baselineFollowup, the old comparison logic)?

If a finding overlaps another dimension's territory, note the overlap in one line rather than re-developing it.

content.text: Based on my review, I'm reporting three findings, ranked by severity.

findings.title: graftSkillContent's multi-step git plumbing has no crash-recovery marker, unlike the merge/revert states it sits next to
findings.scenario: graftSkillContent replaces the old atomic `git merge --no-ff` (chemin A) with a sequence of separate subprocess calls — `git rm -r`, `git checkout <branch> -- <skill>/`, `git add -A`, `git write-tree`, `git commit-tree` — and only reaches an atomic, clean state at the very last `git reset --hard <commitSha>`. Every INTERNAL git failure inside this sequence is caught (`gitTry`/try-catch) and followed by `git reset --hard mainSha`, so logical failures are fine. But if the parent Node process is interrupted between any two of these steps by something the function's own error handling can never run (SIGKILL, OOM, redeploy, host crash — all explicitly treated as ordinary hazards elsewhere in this same file, e.g. the round-3 fixes for merge/revert), the shared `target.integrationClone` is left with uncommitted, staged changes under `<skill>/` and no git-native in-progress marker (no MERGE_HEAD/REVERT_HEAD). The NEXT call to `mergeApprovedBranchIntoMain` (line 671) or `revertMergeCommitOnMain` (line 771) starts with `abortMergeBestEffort`/`abortRevertBestEffort` — which only recognize merge-in-progress and revert-in-progress states — then does a raw (non-`gitTry`) `git(['checkout', '-B', 'main', 'origin/main'], ...)`. Since the leftover staged content for `<skill>/` differs from `origin/main`'s version (that's the whole point of the graft), git refuses the checkout ("local changes would be overwritten") and this call throws uncaught. `applyApproved`/`applyProposal` do not wrap this call in try/catch, so the exception propagates past the `rebase_needed`+chip fallback this file uses for every other expected failure — crashing the whole apply/revert invocation instead of degrading gracefully. Because `WORKSTATION_SKILLS_INTEGRATION_CLONE` is one shared clone for ALL skills (chemin A), this blocks apply/revert for every proposal on every skill sharing it, with no automatic recovery (no code path ever runs `git reset --hard`/`git clean -fd` on a stale, non-merge dirty tree) until a human manually inspects and cleans the clone by hand. This is a narrower recurrence, inside the new code, of exactly the defect class this chantier exists to close: a mid-operation crash leaving the repo in a half-mutated state with no escape hatch. No sibling elsewhere in this file (grep for `git clean`) establishes a pattern for recovering from this kind of dirty state, so nothing else already covers it either.
findings.suggestedFix: Give `mergeApprovedBranchIntoMain`/`revertMergeCommitOnMain` a best-effort recovery step that also handles a plain dirty/staged working tree left by an interrupted graft — e.g. `gitTry(['reset', '--hard', 'HEAD'])` + `gitTry(['clean', '-fd', '--', skillPath-or-whole-tree])` before the `checkout -B`, mirroring `abortMergeBestEffort`/`abortRevertBestEffort`'s "always safe, never throws" shape — or make the raw `checkout -B` call itself a `gitTry` with a fallback that force-discards local changes when nothing legitimate is in progress. Add a regression test that kills/interrupts a graft mid-sequence (leaves the clone with staged `<skill>/` changes, no commit) and asserts the next `applyProposal`/`revertProposal` call degrades to `rebase_needed` instead of throwing.

findings.title: wakeReason still misses the second-brain-bridge closing signal (agentFollowupStatus:'handled'), so convo watch spins to timeout on externally-resolved conversations
findings.scenario: This diff rewrites `wakeReason` to be "a pure function of the current snapshot" and its docstring frames the rewrite as now correctly detecting genuine completion, fixing both known races. But it still checks only `status === 'completed'` and (new) `computeStatus(items) === 'completed'` — never `agentFollowupStatus === 'handled'`. That third value is how the codebase's own canonical "is this conversation done" predicate, `isConversationOpen` (src/types/conversation.ts:549-553), and its real consumers (server/services/hubPulse.ts:73-80, server/services/triageScan.ts:73-77, server/services/activity.ts:100) already treat a conversation as closed: an approval resolved OUTSIDE the hub by the second-brain bridge's "raccord A" (RA-AC-18, a real, actively-used subsystem — see data/conversations/second-brain/*.json, data/tasks/second-brain/second-brain-bridge.json) never gets its items answered (the identity guard forbids that write path from authoring a response), so `status` stays 'pending'/'in_progress' forever and `computeStatus(items)` never returns 'completed' either. Per the decision_hub protocol (CLAUDE.md), `bun run convo watch` is launched right after every `convo create`. Any hub conversation later resolved via the second-brain bridge instead of the workstation UI is therefore invisible to `wakeReason`: `convo watch` runs out its full 120-minute timeout and reports `VERDICT: TIMEOUT` / exit 2, even though the conversation is genuinely resolved and every other part of the app already treats it as closed. The rewritten docs/decision-hub.md section (~165-197) makes the same omission, describing the two checked signals without mentioning this third, pre-existing, already-documented closing path.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `if (c.agentFollowupStatus === 'handled') return 'completed';` (or a distinct WakeReason variant) to `wakeReason`, mirroring `isConversationOpen`'s three-way check, and add a unit test exercising a conversation with `status: 'pending'`, unanswered items, and `agentFollowupStatus: 'handled'` (the raccord-A shape) to confirm `convo watch` wakes instead of timing out. Update docs/decision-hub.md's enumeration of VERDICT causes to mention this third path.

The new test's own comment acknowledges this is unchanged/out of scope ('comportement inchangé, ce n'est PAS ce que ce fix retire'), so this is a known, accepted gap rather than a hidden one, but it is a real state-inconsistency worth tracking.
findings.suggestedFix: When a retryable item succeeds on a later `cmdImport` after a prior failure created a fallback chip for the same itemKey/skill, either dismiss that chip automatically (if its id/reference can be recovered) or have the chip's prompt note that a later automatic retry may have already resolved it, so a human triaging chips doesn't act on stale information.
